sections.content:
In Twilight doctrine, the canon refers to the commonly accepted dogmas of the [[Church of Twilight]]. It's centred around the two entities known as [[Mother Light]] and [[Mother Night]].

The main deific entities of the Canon are far older than the church, and they make their appearance, though distorted in every mayor religion known in the realm. They are considered so great, that few are the devout followers that dare worship them on a personal level on the daily.

Apart from the few occasions in which the mothers are the main foci of the rituals, the followers of the Canon tend to devout themselves to improve in the image of some saint. This however has a subjective aspect to it, as different cultures have a rather distinct interpretations of the same saints. And some of them (mostly the ones recently added to the canon) only are worshipped in certain regions.

sections.content:
Mother Night is one of the prime deities of the Canon of Twilight. Her original name in druntongue, Shar, has long been forgotten, and only in the most ancient of texts she is referred to by this name.

In contrast to her wife, Mother Night is generally associated with the rules of society and of nature itself, she is considered the judge of souls and the one who helps guide the souls of the departed towards their afterlives. The teachings of the Nightbringer are directed towards justice and protection, with her main commandment being "Give mercy to those who deserve it, and strike swiftly those who don't", and thus she has great importance in both the military foundation of the church and it's justice system. She is also invoked directly in funerary rites to guide the souls of the dead.

Mother Night is often depicted as a woman of white porcelain skin, her age inscrutable behind her stoic, cold stare and pursed lips. Her long black hair falling straight into a black straight dress sparsely adorned.

When she is depicted in her humanoid-like form, she is often clad in silvery armor, holding a sword in one hand and a scale in the other. Otherwise, her most common symbols are the scales, the moon and the raven.

sections.content:
Mother Light is one of the prime deities of the Canon of Twilight. Her original name in druntongue, Selûne, has long been forgotten, and only in the most ancient of texts she is referred to by this name.

Within the pair of greater deities, Mother Light is generally considered the more nurturing and carefree of the two, and her role as the main motor behind growth and life place her in a fundamental role as the recipient of worship in rural communities, more focused on the day to day and prone to live peaceful lives, finding beauty in the small things and celebrating her holy light as she watches over her creatures and cares for peace and happiness.

Those who decide to dedicate their lives to the service of the Dawn Mother generally do so within their communities, as spiritual leaders and healers, relieving whatever suffering they can, and showing compassion and kindness to those in need.

Mother Light is often depicted as a middle aged woman of tanned skin, with golden locks cascading over her shoulders. She usually wears a warm smile on her face and is dressed in white ethereal robes that flow along her curves. 

Although the humanoid-like representations of Mother Light are scarce, she is often signified by the sun, a white dove or a spike of wheat. Generally speaking, her cult is focused on life, fertility, beauty, peace, home and community.

Saint Catalina Obsides was a woman from [[Astoria]] that partook in the [[Holy Wars of Therastur]]. She founded the militant order of the [[Knights of the Everburning Star]], sensing the growing overreaches of mageborn in the southern kingdoms and heralded to battle at the worst of the holy wars. She died a martyr in the battlefield fighting the hoards of undead in order to get the civilians out of the [[County of Dawnmire]].

As she was a renowned general in the war there are multiple portraits of her, which are usually used in her cult. Catalina was a dark skinned woman with white hair and golden eyes, that was said to be a saint from birth and took upon her to fight with extreme zealotry against the last sorcerer king of [[Noorderventer]].

Saint Catherine is the saint patron of law and justice, called now the evening judge she used to have another title in life, The Witch Hunter General. She was infamous amongst the mageborn in the time before the [[Accords of Fendras]], and founded the [[The Night's Inquisition]] later renamed 'The Moon Templars', one of the most notable institutions in the [[Church of Twilight]]. She is also the first recorded woman of power in the church to have married another clergywoman — though the practice predated the church — which would set a precedent for the organization.

Saint Catherine is usually depicted in her holy armaments, all of which have been preserved as relics of the church, and while some of them were lost during the [[Holy Wars of Therastur]], there are extensive records of all of them, including her battleaxe [[Sorcerer's End]], her [[scales]], her [[Darksteel Armor]], her [[Inquisitor's Cloak]] and the crossbow [[Lookout]]. She was a dark skinned woman with a towering height of 6.5 feet but her face is usually hidden behind her cloak, though some of the older statues show her features.

Saint Cecilia was a Kadeshian woman who spearheaded the signage of the [[Accords of Fendras]]. She was the first Lady of Radiance, and architect of the [[Diarchy of Mù Shěng]] as it's known today, marrying her Mistress of Stars [[Zheng Jingyi]], a devout inquisitor using the popular story of [[Saint Catherine]] to legitimize her theocracy. It's said that Cecilia saw visions of the future and used it to amass power and to accomplish peace between the mageborn and the church, creating a purposefully one sided deal that skirted her ambitions. She was said to be pasionate and bolsterous and devoted to her wife with a fervor rivaling her faith.

There are enough depictions of Saint Cecilia to fill several books. Though her more modern representations tend to focus on her more regal appearance — wielding her holy rod and a diamond encrusted tiara — and her blind eyes said to shed tears of pure light, historical paintings — most of which she commissioned herself — are extremely amorous, wether embracing her wife or lounging on her lap. The common features in both of these are the flowing silk tunics, her sunkissed skin and her luscious long and wavy brunette mane.

Saint Charity is the saint patron of the suffering. She was the first matriarch of the [[Church of Twilight]], and during the first years of [[Astoria]], she was said to perform great miracles taking the pain and suffering of the devout and placing it unto her shoulders. Her final miracle was the resurrection of her husband, which took her life, and was later the reason for her canonization.

Saint Charity is usually depicted as an older woman covered in robes, always sitting cross legged and generally holding somebody to her chest. Most often than not this is representative of the figure of her husband.

When the first settlers came to Mercia, it was said that they were godless and believed in the spirits of nature, such as the thunder or the rain. However when they fell prey to the demons that freely walked the land then, their gods didn't protect them, there was no way they could, as fiends burnt their farmlands and sequestered their kin to consume their flesh, the first settlers were left alone. One young woman, named Cristina was amongst these settlers, and in the darkest of night, while she prayed for anyone to listen she heard a voice. Their kind believed in deities but heard their voice in the wind and the fire, never deep within their souls, so Cristina was wary of the voice, thinking it another fiend going after her soul.

The voice was firm and calm, and devoid of any deceit, and told the young girl of an artifact that would ensue the survival of her people, would she wield it, but that warned her that to get it she would need to show devotion and bravery to the point of madness. She told her of the location, and with newfound hope, Cristina travelled through the mountains into the unknown, until she found a temple whereupon she found a shield.

After a few weeks, as she returned to her homestead, she found the land ravaged, and the few survivors, cowering as they told her of the terrors bumping in the night, and how they wouldn't survive the night, as every day their dead woke up and rose alongside the fiends. However once night came, Cristina rose her golden shield, shinning with the light of a million stars and despite the wounds and burns overcoming her body, she rose her shield from dusk to dawn and repelled the demons.

For a year and a day, Cristina continued to rise her shield, as her kin fired arrows at the demons, and until the last one was gone, she never fell, nor did she show any doubt. But once her task was done, the pain finally overcame her. As her disfigured body exhaled her last breath, those around saw clearly an angel pick her soul out of her body and carry her towards the stars.

She is generally depicted as a young woman of dark hair and her body is generally covered, in order to hide the wounds of her sacrifice. Some gruesome depictions show her disfigured face and her burned hair. She is usually shown either fighting off demons or protecting people, but the only consistent feature is her silver shield.

Saint Clara is one of the most mysterious figures of Twilight doctrine. There is candid debate on whether she ever was a mortal woman, something that even caused the first schism within the church. She is said to have been amonst the first settlers, though some versions of the myth portray her as waiting for the settlers at the shores of what would become [[Cannalis]]. There are a multitude of myths related to her, though which are true if any is impossible to tell: - She single handedly slain the great wyrm Al'tiniyn Al'rahib with her silver bow. - She went into the darkwoods, enamoured the queen of the dark forests ensuring the protection of the forests to the south. - She went into the wildlands and brough back several artifacts of the mothers. - She protected the city of flowers from a demonic host, pushing the devils into hell and crossing with them. Regardless of which of these stories is considered canonical at a given time, any of them ending with her death or chaining to the Auldwoods is enough to consider her a saint. Many become charmed by her heroic deeds and devote their lives to emulate the glorious figure.

Most contemporary depictions of Saint Clara center her consecration or swearing to the ideals of the Twilight. She is often a faceless woman clad in silver armor with a sword and shield, though earlier depictions sometimes show her with a silver bow.

metadata.Titles: Guardian of the Crossroads, Guide to Lost Souls

sections.content: Saint Clementia is the saint of crossroads and travellers. She is said to be the angel that guides the lost souls to their afterlife. Saint Clementia is said to predate the discovery of the faith by the first settlers and believed to have been the one to guide them to the continent of Mercia, however, the most zealous postulate that she was an actual person, who guided the ships of the first settlers.

Saint Clementia is generally depicted as a middle aged woman with 3 pairs of angelic wings on her back that carries a crook on one hand and an oil lantern in the other. She is usually accompanied by a dog and wears the vestments of a simple cleric of the [[Church of Twilight]].
